label: Around the delimiter (last original token / <DEL> / first copy step) at absolute t=8-10 in sequences starting with c or o
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.016% of steps). Its activations sit in a narrow window around the delimiter: the last original token, the <DEL> step, and the first copy step (recall_idx 0-1). It fires almost only in long sequences (L=8-9, about 88% of mass) at absolute steps t=8-10, and never at t<5. It is strongly gated on the first original token: first_tok c (15x lift, 52% of mass) or o (9x lift, 28%). When the input itself is o (11x lift), it fires whatever the first token is. The strongest examples begin with c, and in them the feature is active on several consecutive steps from the last original tokens through <DEL> to the copy-phase input c. It does not fire early in the original phase, in short sequences, or later in the copy phase. The context predicate covers about two thirds of the activation mass, but its precision is only about 2%: most steps matching this context stay silent. Adding history conditions (which tokens appear in the sequence) did not substantially sharpen it, so the deciding factor is not captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=c (+4.24), in_tok=o (+3.54), phase=2 & in_tok=3 (+2.91), prev_tok=z (+2.73), prev_tok=<DEL> (+2.67), prev_tok=x (+2.58). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.68), phase=2 (-1.77), orig8=- (-1.30), orig7=- (-0.81).
